messages.subject: effective strip width
parts:
I'm reviewing a paper where the authors simply calculated the effective
strip width and then multiplied the number of ALL BIRDS (out to all
distances including those beyond the ESW) by the area surveyed within the
ESW by transect length. It seems to me that this would report the same
density or overall population size as DISTANCE but bot report any error
values.

Any thoughts?

thanks,

messages.author: 4b4a7b00c1dd09c7
messages.subject: Re: effective strip width
parts:
Hi Ben (and distance list),

Yes, you're right, assuming they didn't truncate some of the data at the
analysis stage to estimate their ESW.

If they did truncate, then density is number of birds seen **within the
truncation boundary** divided by the effective search area. (Effective search
area is 2 x total transect length x ESW.)

- Len
